meta.search_description: Light roast from a family farm near Acevedo, Huila, Colombia: red grape, panela and orange zest. $24.00 for 340 g.
meta.search_title: Huila Pink Bourbon coffee beans, Prairie Ash
meta.story_body: This Pink Bourbon grows at 1,750 m on a family farm near Acevedo in Huila. We have bought from the same family since our first harvest. The cherries are picked ripe, fermented for 36 hours, washed and dried on raised beds for about three weeks.

meta.search_description: Light roast from a washing station near Bensa, Sidama, Ethiopia: jasmine, bergamot and white peach. $25.00 for 340 g.
meta.search_title: Sidama Bensa coffee beans, Prairie Ash
meta.story_body: Smallholders around Bensa deliver ripe cherries to one washing station at 2,000 m. The coffee is fermented for 48 hours, washed and dried on raised beds for about two weeks. We have bought this lot for three harvests.

meta.search_description: Our house espresso of Cerrado and Huila: milk chocolate, hazelnut and cherry. $21.00 for 340 g, $56.00 for 1 kg.
meta.search_title: Exchange House Espresso, Prairie Ash
meta.story_body: Our house blend: a natural coffee from the Cerrado for body and sweetness, and a washed Huila for the cherry. Mara blends it after roasting, two parts Cerrado to one part Huila.

meta.search_title: Huila Sugarcane Decaf coffee beans, Prairie Ash
meta.story_body: Washed coffee from Huila, decaffeinated near the farm with ethyl acetate made from fermented sugarcane, which keeps the sweetness of the bean.

meta.search_description: Medium roast from the highlands of Huehuetenango, Guatemala: toffee, almond and plum. $22.00 for 340 g.
meta.search_title: Huehuetenango coffee beans, Prairie Ash
meta.story_body: Grown at about 1,800 m in the highlands of Huehuetenango, where warm air from the Mexican lowlands keeps frost off the farms. Washed and sun dried on patios.

meta.search_description: Light roast from Kirinyaga, Kenya: blackcurrant, grapefruit and cane sugar. Back after Friday's roast, $27.00 for 340 g.
meta.search_title: Kirinyaga coffee beans, Prairie Ash
meta.story_body: Smallholders on the slopes of Mount Kenya deliver cherries to a cooperative washing station at about 1,700 m. Double fermented, washed and dried on raised beds.
